definitions.explanation: Describes something that is physically or temporally very far away. Often evokes a poetic or wistful tone.
Used to emphasize a large difference in degree when making comparisons.

examples.japanese: {遥|はる}か{遠|とお}くに{山|やま}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: Mountains are visible far in the distance.

examples.japanese: {遥|はる}か{昔|むかし}のことだ。
examples.english: That was a long, long time ago.

examples.japanese: {空港|くうこう}から{遥|はる}かに{続|つづ}く{砂漠|さばく}を{眺|なが}めた。
examples.english: I gazed at the desert stretching far beyond the airport.

examples.japanese: こっちの{方|ほう}が{遥|はる}かにいい。
{実際|じっさい}は{予想|よそう}より{遥|はる}かに{難|むずか}しかった。
examples.english: In reality, it was far more difficult than expected.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{料理|りょうり}は、あの{店|みせ}より{遥|はる}かにおいしい。
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is far better than at that one.

notes:
{遥|はる}か can function as both an adverb and a na-adjective.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {遥|はる}か{遠|とお}く: far in the distance
- {遥|はる}か{昔|むかし}: a long time ago
- {遥|はる}かに + comparative: far more ~, by far ~
- {遥|はる}かな + noun: distant ~, far-off ~

USAGE: When modifying a noun directly, use the na-adjective form ({遥|はる}かな). When modifying a verb or adjective, use the adverbial form ({遥|はる}かに). The word often carries a literary or poetic nuance, evoking a sense of longing or vastness.
